messages:
sam: Anyone else seeing terraform apply hang after importing the cert secret? I ran import then plan looked fine but apply never finishes.
mira: saw something similar last week with rotated certs, what error do you get?
sam: apply just sits at "Refreshing state..." for a long time then errors out:
```
Error: Provider produced inconsistent result after apply

When applying changes to aws_secretsmanager_secret_version.cert, the provider reported the resource as created, but with an inconsistent state.
This is usually caused by provider-side defaults and should be fixed by refreshing the state.
```
kai: hmm, did you import both the secret and the secret version? we had a case where the secret meta and version didn't match so plan wanted to recreate.
sam: I imported secret with `terraform import module.secrets.aws_secretsmanager_secret.prod cert-abc123` then tried apply. I didn't import the version.
mira: try `terraform import module.secrets.aws_secretsmanager_secret_version.prod prod/1` (use the proper version id) or delete the orphaned state entry if the version should be managed outside TF.
opsbot: deploy-bot: apply started by @sam in staging (run id: run-9042) :hourglass_flowing_sand:
kai: also check for state locks in the backend. run `terraform force-unlock -force LOCK_ID` only if you're sure no one else is running applies. we had a stale lock after a failed import.
sam: run shows remote state ok, no active locks. output of `terraform state list | grep cert` shows the secret but not the version.
mira: ok that matches. if the resource in TF references attributes that only come from the version, plan may attempt to recreate. Either import the version or change the config to stop referencing version-specific attrs.
sam: curious — would `terraform state mv` help to move the resource under a slightly different address?
kai: state mv won't fix mismatched resource shape. Import the exact resource the config expects. If the provider returns different computed defaults on create vs read, you may need a `terraform refresh` then apply.
sam: did a refresh, still same error. plan shows recreate: `-/+ aws_secretsmanager_secret_version.prod (new resource required)`
mira: another trick: create a temporary minimal config that matches the current remote shape, import into that address, run refresh, then update back to the real config and run a targeted state mv/import. messy but works when provider defaults change during create.
opsbot: note: CI auto-apply disabled while we debug, re-enable after patch.
sam: thanks — I'll try importing the version and if that fails try the temporary-config workflow. pinging @mira if I need help with the import id extraction. :thumbsup:
mira: happy to pair if needed. also file a short doc in eng-infra/terraform-runbooks about this import/version mismatch pattern so we don't repeat it.
sam: will do, logging notes now.
